note: `vpcm_run`, the V.PCM datapump's `.process`.  It is not the modem: it is a block quantiser, two sample queues, a bit pipe in both directions and a seventeen-arm dispatch, with the whole of V.34, V.90, V.92 and K56Flex behind one call to `VPcmV34Progress` (findings F980, F982).  So what this set has to prove is that the queueing arithmetic is driven, that the bit pipe carries in both directions and remembers its count, that the dispatch fires on a CHANGE and the connect report on a TRANSITION, and that the connect arm tells the host the right two things in the right order.  The binary is `t_vpcmrun`, the four-way comparison of a connecting V.34 call (finding F984); `t_vpcmguard` is the other half of the function and has its own set.

THE FIVE EQUIVALENTS ARE THE POINT OF THIS SET, AND FOUR OF THEM ARE ONE FACT.  The host contract fixes `count` at `m->frag` == 48 (finding F964, vpcm.h), 48 is a multiple of four and the input queue is empty on every block, so `nproc` is identically `count`, both input residues are identically zero and `in` is never rebound.  That makes the input queue dead code on every driver `slmodemd` has -- and a driver whose `frag` is not a multiple of four turns all four CAUGHT, which is exactly the alarm wanted and does not otherwise exist.  Finding F1000.

THREE ROWS OF FINDING F987'S TABLE ARE WRONG AND THIS SET IS WHY THEY WERE FOUND.  The OUTPUT queue is not dead: `outq.count` is a constant FOUR, not zero, so the compaction moves four samples every block and dropping it is CAUGHT (finding F1001).  The mute path is not unexercised: `vpcm_create` seeds the counter at 528 and the first eleven blocks of every call are silenced (finding F1002).  And `fout` holds whole numbers on every sample of all 8,000 blocks, so a SYMMETRIC rounding rule cannot be seen while an unconditional `+0.5` is caught at once -- the conversion's direction is pinned and its rounding rule is not observable here (finding F1003).

THE TWO STALL MUTATIONS ARE UNCAUGHT AND NOT EQUIVALENT.  Both change behaviour for inputs the host contract permits -- nothing else resets `stall`, and the deadline is a specific block count -- so the reason they survive is that this call's trajectory never accumulates 3,000 unchanged code-0 blocks.  That is `the test does not cover it`, which mutate.py's docstring puts in the uncaught list rather than dressing up as an argument about the code.

Measured as well as argued: a probe asserting `nproc == 48` and one asserting `s->inq.count == 0` both survive the whole 8,000-block run.  The `/4*4` and the signed fixup the object pays for at 0x4187 are unreachable arithmetic on every driver `slmodemd` has, and a `frag` that is not a multiple of four makes this CAUGHT.

why: The guard is `pending + count != nproc` and the copy's length is `pending + count - nproc` -- the same quantity tested and then used.  With `count` == 48 the quantisation above is exact, so that quantity is identically zero: the guard is false on every block and the body it guards would be a memcpy of zero bytes if it ever ran.  This removes a branch that is never taken, not a copy that ever moves a sample, and `s->inq.count` is still assigned so the queue's own state is untouched.

why: `in` is rebound to `s->inq.buf` in exactly one place, under `if (pending > 0)`, and `pending` is `s->inq.count`, which the tail leaves at zero on every block for the reason above. label: the receive bit mask is dropped
why: `& 1` is the identity on 0 and 1, and `rxbits` holds one BIT per int -- `VPcmV34Progress`'s contract in vpcm.h is `*nrx` bits recovered, and `modem_put_bits` is called with a width of 1 -- so the mask can only alter a value the callee is not permitted to produce.  THIS ONE RESTS ON A MEASUREMENT OF THE CALLEE rather than on arithmetic: a probe asserting `(s->rxbits[i] & ~1) == 0` over every recovered bit of the 8,000 blocks survives, so the range is measured and not assumed.  It stops holding the moment `VPcmV34Main.cpp` is reconstructed differently.

label: float -> short rounds half away from zero rather than truncating
why: Every value `VPcmV34Progress` writes into `fout` is a WHOLE NUMBER: a probe asserting `s->fout[i] == (float)(int)s->fout[i]` survives all 8,000 blocks, as does one asserting that truncation and round-half-away return the same short for every sample.  On an integral value every SYMMETRIC rounding rule and truncation agree, so no test can separate them -- which is a fact about the values the code converts, not about the checks.  The direction is still pinned: the companion mutation adding an unconditional `+0.5f` is CAUGHT, because that is not symmetric and moves every negative whole number by one.  So the pair says the object's `fnstcw / or $0xc00 / fistps` is a truncation towards zero and not a biased round, and says the rest is unobservable here.
